department: Department of Materials Science and Engineering

deadline.value: Apply by December 1, 2026, 8:59 pm Pacific; all materials are due by then.
deadline.quote: Doctor of Philosophy (MS/Ph.D., Ph.D.) December 1, 2026 8:59 pm, Pacific Standard Time

gre_general.value: The GRE is optional but highly recommended for Fall 2027 entry; it becomes required from Fall 2028 entry.
gre_general.quote: The GRE is optional but highly recommended for the 2026-27 admissions cycle, for program entry August 2027. Starting with admissions cycle 2027-28 (for program entry August 2028) the GRE will be required.

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for this field; ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Applicants are encouraged to contact faculty about joining their groups as research assistants, but this is not required to apply.
supervisor.quote: Applicants and admitted students are encouraged to contact faculty in your areas of research interest to discuss the possibility of joining their groups as a GSR.

funding.value: The vast majority of PhD students have tuition, fees, insurance and a stipend covered (research or teaching appointments, fellowships).
funding.quote: the vast majority of our graduate students working (ultimately) towards their Ph.D. will have their tuition, campus fees, insurance, and stipend covered for them.

entry_route.value: A bachelor's in engineering, physics, chemistry or a related field (conferred before enrolment) is required; you can enter the MS/PhD or PhD directly.
entry_route.quote: A bachelor’s degree or recognized equivalent (must be conferred prior to enrollment into our program) from an accredited institution in Engineering, Physics or Chemistry, or related field is required.

notes: MSE asks for a minimum GPA of 3.2. Its TOEFL/IELTS text still refers to older test dates; follow the Graduate Division rules.
